title: Evaluating Passing Performance in Youth Football: A Systematic Review Toward an Ecological Dynamics Framework
venue: Journal of Sports Science and Medicine
abstract: Passing is a fundamental component of football performance, yet current approaches to evaluating passing performance in youth football remain methodologically diverse and conceptually fragmented. This systematic review aimed to map and critically evaluate existing approaches to evaluating passing performance in youth football, focusing on evaluation dimensions, indicators, tools, scenarios, and the extent to which individual, task, and environmental constraints are reported or incorporated. The review also aimed to synthesize the evidence toward a conceptual micro-meso-macro framework for representative passing evaluation. A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus was conducted for peer-reviewed studies published between January 2000 and September 2025 involving youth association football players aged 19 years or younger and reporting passing-related outcomes. Studies were selected according to predefined eligibility criteria and reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Methodological and reporting quality was assessed using a 16-item checklist, and included studies were coded using an individual-task-environment constraint framework. The review protocol was registered in the Open Science Framework before database searching, screening, data extraction, ecological coding, and synthesis (OSF registration ID: 2bqfy). Thirty-six studies were included. The reviewed approaches were organized into three analytical dimensions: individual technical ability, contextual decision-making ability, and passing team contribution. Contextual decision-making represented the largest group of studies, whereas team contribution approaches were less frequently represented. title: Aportes de la educación física a la construcción de competencias ciudadanas en básica secundaria
abstract: Resumen La formación de competencias ciudadanas constituye un desafío para las instituciones educativas, especialmente frente a la necesidad de promover relaciones basadas en el reconocimiento del otro, la convivencia y la participación. Más allá del mero aprendizaje memorístico de reglas y conceptos, demanda la creación de vivencias escolares participativas donde el estudiantado ejerza la toma de decisiones, la resolución de divergencias y el cultivo de vínculos interpersonales significativos. El presente estudio tuvo como propósito general construir una sustentación teórica sobre el aporte de la educación física al desarrollo de las competencias ciudadanas en estudiantes de básica secundaria en Colombia. Se desarrolló desde el paradigma interpretativo, enfoque cualitativo, mediante el diseño fenomenológico y la hermenéutica. Participaron cuatro docentes de educación física, cuyas narrativas fueron abordadas mediante categorización, estructuración, saturación y triangulación. Los resultados permitieron configurar tres categorías teorizadoras: la corporeidad como ontología del ser ciudadano en el espacio escolar; la praxiología de la corporeidad como escenario de formación política y ética desde la educación física; y la resignificación pedagógica del discurso declarativo hacia la vivencia relacional. Los hallazgos evidencian que la educación física constituye un espacio de interacción donde el cuerpo, la motricidad, la alteridad, la regulación emocional y la experiencia compartida favorecen procesos de formación ciudadana. Se concluye que su contribución trasciende el desarrollo físico y requiere una mediación pedagógica intencionada que articule corporeidad, convivencia, reflexión y participación ciudadana.

title: Protocolo de prevenção à violência desportiva da Polícia Militar de Pernambuco: relato de experiência após o ataque à delegação do Fortaleza Esporte Clube
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: O ataque à delegação do Fortaleza Esporte Clube, em fevereiro de 2024, no Recife, expôs a vulnerabilidade de comitivas e caravanas em trânsito e levou a Polícia Militar de Pernambuco (PMPE) a reformular seus procedimentos em jogos de futebol. Este relato de experiência tem como objetivo descrever e analisar criticamente a concepção e a aplicação do protocolo de prevenção à violência desportiva então construído, a partir da participação do autor na equipe de planejamento operacional. A experiência foi fundamentada na literatura sobre violência no futebol, prevenção situacional e atividade de inteligência, e confrontada com dados da Coordenação de Inteligência da PMPE (2020 a 2026) e do sistema Infopol, da Secretaria de Defesa Social. O protocolo estruturou-se em cinco pilares: escolta de delegações, posicionamento estratégico de viaturas, vigilância continuada, aproximação institucional com lideranças de torcidas e reforço da inteligência. Após o pico de 23 registros de confrontos entre torcidas organizadas em 2024, houve redução para 16 em 2025 e para 9 em 2026, ano ainda parcial; desde a implantação do protocolo, registrou-se um único ataque a delegação, sem feridos; e os crimes de intolerância esportiva registrados pela delegacia especializada diminuíram 21,05% em relação ao período anterior. Conclui-se que os resultados são compatíveis com a efetividade do protocolo, embora a série curta e a ausência de grupo de comparação impeçam afirmar relação causal, e que a experiência oferece subsídios a outras corporações policiais.

title: Objective Internal Load
abstract: Objective internal load represents the measurable physiological stress imposed by training and competition. In team sports, the combination of intermittent high-intensity running, repeated accelerations and decelerations, rapid changes of direction, technical–tactical constraints, and in some sports, frequent collisions produces large within-session fluctuations and between-day variability in cardiovascular and autonomic responses. Heart rate (HR) remains the most widely implemented objective internal-load signal because it is non-invasive, scalable across squads, and easily integrated with exposure time to derive interpretable indices such as time-in-zone and training impulse (TRIMP). In parallel, resting and recovery measures including heart rate variability (HRV), standardized submaximal-exercise HR, and post-exercise HR recovery provide complementary information on readiness, adaptation, and maladaptation when measured under standardized conditions, interpreted against individual baselines, and triangulated with external load, subjective tools, and contextual factors. This chapter summarizes the physiological rationale, acquisition and quality-control requirements, and interpretive frameworks for HR-derived internal-load monitoring in team sports, with applied examples from soccer, rugby, basketball, and hockey. Practical recommendations are provided for device selection, data-quality assurance, standardization of measurement conditions, and decision thresholds that support daily decision-making in high-performance environments.

title: Technical-Tactical Load
abstract: Technical-tactical load refers to the context-dependent demands imposed by sport-specific technical actions, tactical coordination, perceptual information pickup, and decision-making under task, environmental, and interpersonal constraints. This chapter analyzes how technical-tactical demands emerge across structured drills, small-sided and conditioned games, and official competition contexts. Evaluation methods such as notational analysis, decision analysis, and new approaches based on artificial intelligence or machine learning are addressed. The relationship between physical load and cognitive load is discussed, as well as the need to integrate this dimension in training planning. Practical examples of how tasks with high tactical demand can influence physical and mental performance are presented, and strategies are offered to measure and control this load, optimizing both the preparation and the transfer to the competitive environment.

title: Application of Internal and External Load Monitoring Variables
abstract: The correct interpretation and application of internal and external load data is essential to optimize performance, reduce the risk of injury, and facilitate decision-making in real sporting contexts. This chapter offers an integrative view of how to practically implement the different metrics obtained in the monitoring process. It addresses the design of efficient monitoring systems based on the collection, analysis, and visualization of individualized and contextual data. In addition, examples of how to interpret fluctuations in load to support decisions on training volume, intensity, and content are presented. Load response models (such as the fitness-fatigue model) are also analyzed, and the need for establishing personalized baseline values and alert values is discussed. Finally, a functional structure is proposed to integrate these metrics into the day-to-day operations of sports teams, aligning performance objectives with athlete health and well-being.

title: Dynamics of tactical behaviour in association football when manipulating players' space of interaction
abstract: The analysis of positional data in association football allows the spatial distribution of players during matches to be described in order to improve the understanding of tactical-related constraints on the behavioural dynamics of players. The aim of this study was to identify how players' spatial restrictions affected the exploratory tactical behaviour and constrained the perceptual-motor workspace of players in possession of the ball, as well as inter-player passing interactions. Nineteen professional outfield male players were divided into two teams of 10 and 9 players, respectively. The game was played under three spatial constraints: a) players were not allowed to move out of their allocated zones, except for the player in possession of the ball; b) players were allowed to move to an adjacent zone, and; c) non-specific spatial constraints. Positional data was captured using a 5 Hz interpolated GPS tracking system and used to define the configuration states of players for each second in time. The configuration state comprised 37 categories derived from tactical actions, distance from the nearest opponent, distance from the target and movement speed. Notational analysis of players in possession of the ball allowed the mean time of ball possession and the probabilities of passing the ball between players to be calculated. The results revealed that the players' long-term exploratory behaviour decreased and their short-term exploration increased when restricting their space of interaction. Relaxing players' positional constraints seemed to increase the speed of ball flow dynamics. title: The tactics of successful attacks in professional association football: large-scale spatiotemporal analysis of dynamic subgroups using position tracking data
abstract: Association football teams can be considered complex dynamical systems of individuals grouped in subgroups (defenders, midfielders and attackers), coordinating their behaviour to achieve a shared goal. As research often focusses on collective behaviour, or on static subgroups, the current study aims to analyse spatiotemporal behaviour of dynamic subgroups in relation to successful attacks. We collected position tracking data of 118 Dutch Eredivisie matches, containing 12424 attacks. Attacks were classified as successful (N = 1237) or non-successful (N = 11187) based on the potential of creating a scoring opportunity. Using unsupervised machine learning, we automatically identified dynamic formations based on position tracking data, and identified dynamic subgroups for every timeframe in a match. We then compared the subgroup centroids to assess the intra- and inter-team spatiotemporal synchronisation during successful and non-successful attacks, using circular statistics. Our results indicated subgroup-level variables provided more information, and were more sensitive to disruption, in comparison to team-level variables. When comparing successful and non-successful attacks, we found decreases (p < .01) in longitudinal inter- and intra-team synchrony of interactions involving the defenders of the attacking team during successful attacks. This study provides the first large-scale dynamic subgroup analysis and reveals additional insights to team-level analyses.

title: Defending in 4-4-2 or 5-3-2 formation? small differences in footballers’ collective tactical behaviours
abstract: This study explored footballers' tactical behaviours, based on their position data, as an effect of two defending formations, 4-4-2 and 5-3-2, using an experimental approach. Sixty-nine youth footballers participated in this 11-versus-11 study, performing 72 trials of attack-versus-defence. Players' position data were tracked using a local positioning system, and processed to calculate measures of collective movement. This was supplemented by the analysis of passing networks. The results showed small differences between the two conditions. Compared to a 4-4-2 formation, defending in 5-3-2 reduced dispersion (-0.69 m,p=0.012), midfield-forward distance (-0.81 m, p=0.047), and defence-forward distance (-1.29 m, p=0.038); the consequent effects on attacking teams included reduced team widths (-1.78 m, p=0.034), reduced necessity for back-passes to the goalkeeper, and less connectivity in the passing network. The effects of the two defending formations seem to have the greatest impact on fullbacks of the attacking teams, since they were main contributors of the reduced team widths, received more passes, and had higher betweenness centrality in the right-back position during 5-3-2 defending. In summary, the present study potentially demonstrates how the underlying mechanisms in players' collective movements and passing behaviours show that the 5-3-2 is more conservatively defensive than the 4-4-2.

title: Collective states and their transitions in football
abstract: Movement, positioning and coordination of player formations is a key aspect for the performance of teams within field-based sports. The increased availability of player tracking data has given rise to numerous studies that focus on the relationship between simple descriptive statistics surrounding team formation and performance. While these existing approaches have provided a high-level a view of team-based spatial formations, there is limited research on the nature of collective movement across players within teams and the establishment of stable collective states within game play. This study draws inspiration from the analysis of collective movement in nature, such as that observed within schools of fish and flocking birds, to explore the existence of collective states within the phases of play in soccer. Order parameters and metrics describing group motion and shape are derived from player movement tracks to uncover the nature of the team's collective states and transitions. This represents a unique addition to the current body of work around the analysis of player movement in team sports. The results from this study demonstrate that sequences of ordered collective behaviours exist with relatively rapid transitions between highly aligned polar and un-ordered swarm behaviours (and vice-versa). Defensive phases of play have a higher proportion of ordered team movement than attacking phases, indicating that movements linked with attacking tactics, such as player dispersion to generate passing and shooting opportunities leads to lower overall collective order. Exploration within this study suggests that defensive tactics, such as reducing the depth or width to close passing opportunities, allows for higher team movement speeds and increased levels of collective order. title: Methodological Procedures for Non-Linear Analyses of Physiological and Behavioural Data in Football
abstract: Complex and dynamic systems are characterised by emergent behaviour, self-similarity, self-organisation and a chaotic component. In team sports as football, complexity and non-linear dynamics includes understanding the mechanisms underlying human movement and collective behaviour. Linear systems approaches in this kind of sports may limit performance understanding due to the fact that small changes in the inputs may not represent proportional and quantifiable changes in the output. Thus, non-linear approaches have been applied to assess training and match outcomes in football. The increasing access to wearable and tracking technology provides large datasets, enabling the analyses of time-series related to different performance indicators such as physiological and positional parameters. However, it is important to frame the theoretical concepts, mathematical models and procedures to determine metrics with physiological and behavioural significance. Additionally, physiological and behavioural data should be considered to determine the complexity and non-linearity of the system in football. Thus, the current chapter summarises the main methodological procedures to extract positional data using non-linear analyses such as entropy scales, relative phase transforms, non-linear indexes, cross correlation, fractals and clustering methods.

title: From Optical Tracking to Tactical Performance via Voronoi Diagrams: Team Formation and Players’ Roles Constrain Interpersonal Linkages in High-Level Football
abstract: Football performance behaviour relies on the individual and collective perceptual attunement to the opportunities for action (affordances) available in a given competitive environment. Such perception-action coupling is constrained by players' spatial dominance. Aiming to understand the influence of team formation and players' roles in their dynamic interaction (interpersonal linkages), Voronoi diagrams were used to assess the differences in players' spatial dominance resulting from their interactions according to ball-possession status in high-performance football. Notational (i.e., team formation, players' role, and ball-possession status) and positional data (from optical sensors) from ten matches of the men's French main football league were analysed. Voronoi diagrams were computed from players' positional data for both teams. Probability density functions of the players' Voronoi cell areas were then computed and compared, using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, for the different variables (i.e., team formation, player role, and ball-possession status) and their classes. For these variables, the players' Voronoi cell areas presented statistical differences, which were sensitive to team formation classes (i.e., defenders, midfielders, and forwards) and relative pitch location (interior or exterior in the effective play space). Differences were also found between players with similar roles when in different team formations. Our results showed that team formation and players' roles constrain their interpersonal linkages, resulting in different spatial dominance patterns. title: Inspecting teammates’ coverage during attacking plays in a football game: A case study
venue: International Journal of Performance Analysis in Sport
abstract: The tactical behaviour of football players is fundamental in sport teams. Despite this importance, the methods to measure such behaviour are very time-consuming for human operators. Therefore, the aim of this case study was to propose a set of collective technological metrics to evaluate the attacking coverage provided by teammates to the player in possession of the ball. For this case study data was collected from three official matches of the same professional team. Using the information about the Cartesian position of players in the field provided from a tracking method, it was possible to propose four different technological metrics and ratios: i) cover in support; ii) cover in vigilance; iii) attacking cover; and iv) depth mobility. Using those metrics it was possible to observe that on average the team observed use with higher regularity support in vigilance as well as depth mobility, thus suggesting a specific tactical behaviour. In summary, it was possible to apply all metrics to real data from three official matches, thus allowing a new technological method to improve the match analysis systems that use multiplayer tracking.

title: Do contextual variables influence the spatial organisations of elite-level Brazilian professional soccer players?
abstract: Purpose. This study investigated the influence of contextual variables on individual and collective team spatial organisation in professional Brazilian players. Methods. Seventeen matches were analysed during the 1st division Brazilian National football League of 2019. Global Positioning System devices were used to track players’ in-game movements. The data were analysed using Matlab to calculate linear tactical variables. The selected tactical variables were ‘Distance from the last defender to the goal’; ‘Width and length’; ‘LpWratio’; ‘Spread’; ‘Space exploration index’ and ‘Stretch index’. Five contextual variables were considered: (i) playing time, (ii) match location, (ii) ranking of the opposition, (iii) match outcome, and (iv) match status. Results. Results demonstrated that the LpWratio values were significantly greater during the second half of matches when compared with the first half (p = 0.03; d = 0.62). Significantly greater length and spread values were identified when the team was playing against a bottom six team when compared with the medium eight teams (p = 0.05; d = 1.58–1.60). Significantly higher stretch index values were reported when playing a top six opposition team when compared with the medium eight opposition teams. During losses, the stretch index was significantly higher when compared with wins and draws, respectively (p = 0.01; d = 1.47–1.89). Finally, the LpWratio values were significantly higher during periods when the team was losing, when compared with periods of drawing and winning (p = 0.01; d = 1.07–1.12). Conclusions. In conclusion, the spatiotemporal organisations of professional-level Brazilian club players are significantly influenced by contextual variables. title: Lifecourse epidemiology of disease: a tractable problem?
abstract: On British television there are many opportunities for time-wasting, but few are as abject as ‘fantasy football’. On the diminishing occasions when it is not possible to track down a televised game to watch, or at least a soap opera about footballers and their wives, teams can be invented and, through a process of weighted averages, compared using the scores from actual games. The sense that humanity is undergoing de-evolution generated by watching this programme is not redeemed by the blather of the presenter, a man whose lack of talent was already clear in 1977 when he was rejected at an audition for the seminal proto-punk band, The Prefects.1 Sometimes not even fantasy football is available to occupy the long summer evenings, but epidemiologists could fill the void by envisaging their fantasy cohort. Imagine you could magic up the perfect study to answer the epidemiological questions you were interested in. Since this issue of the IJE is on lifecourse epidemiology, consider the perfect lifecourse cohort, one up to the task identified by Yoav Ben-Shlomo and Diana Kuh in their definition of lifecourse epidemiology as ‘the study of long-term effects on chronic disease risk of physical and social exposures during gestation, childhood, adolescence, young adulthood and later adult life. It includes studies of the biological, behavioural and psychosocial pathways that operate across an individual's life course, as well as across generations, to influence the development of chronic diseases’.2 The promise of the lifecourse approach is that trajectories to health and disease can be understood at a level of detail that allows for the identification of how and when optimal outcomes can be promoted. title: Reliability of spatial-temporal metrics used to assess collective behaviours in football: an in-silico experiment
abstract: BACKGROUND: The purpose of this study was to investigate the reliability of spatio-temporal measurements applied within collective behaviour research in football. METHODS: In silico experiments were conducted introducing positional errors (0.5, 2 and 4 m) representative of commercial tracking systems to match data from the 2020 European Championship qualifiers. Ratios of the natural variance ('signal') of spatio-temporal metrics obtained throughout sections of each game relative to the variance created by positional errors ('noise') were taken to calculate reliability. The effects of error magnitude and time of analysis (1, 5 and 15 mins; length of attack: 20 s) were assessed and compared using Cohen's f2 effect size. RESULTS: Error magnitude was found to exert greater influence on reliability (f2 = 0.15 to 0.81) compared with both standard time of analysis (f2 = 0.03 to 0.08) and length of attacks (f2 = 0.15 to 0.32). DISCUSSION: The results demonstrate that technologies generating positional errors of 0.5 m or less should be expected to produce spatio-temporal metrics with high reliability. However, technologies that generate errors of 2 m or greater may produce unreliable values, particularly when analyses are conducted over discrete events such as attacks, which although critical, are often short in duration.

title: The Eye in the Sky—A Method to Obtain On-Field Locations of Australian Rules Football Athletes
abstract: The ability to overcome an opposition in team sports is reliant upon an understanding of the tactical behaviour of the opposing team members. Recent research is limited to a performance analysts’ own playing team members, as the required opposing team athletes’ geolocation (GPS) data are unavailable. However, in professional Australian rules Football (AF), animations of athlete GPS data from all teams are commercially available. The purpose of this technical study was to obtain the on-field location of AF athletes from animations of the 2019 Australian Football League season to enable the examination of the tactical behaviour of any team. The pre-trained object detection model YOLOv4 was fine-tuned to detect players, and a custom convolutional neural network was trained to track numbers in the animations. The object detection and the athlete tracking achieved an accuracy of 0.94 and 0.98, respectively. Subsequent scaling and translation coefficients were determined through solving an optimisation problem to transform the pixel coordinate positions of a tracked player number to field-relative Cartesian coordinates. The derived equations achieved an average Euclidean distance from the athletes’ raw GPS data of 2.63 m. The proposed athlete detection and tracking approach is a novel methodology to obtain the on-field positions of AF athletes in the absence of direct measures, which may be used for the analysis of opposition collective team behaviour and in the development of interactive play sketching AF tools.

title: Análisis de rendimiento en el fútbol profesional usando aprendizaje automático
abstract: En los últimos años, el fútbol profesional ha sufrido una gran transformación gracias a la utilización de la tecnología en todos los aspectos de este deporte. La incorporación de herramientas como el análisis de datos, ha sido clave para la optimización del rendimiento de los equipos de fútbol profesionales. Más allá de la intuición y la experiencia de los cuerpos técnicos, los clubes y selecciones nacionales recurren a técnicas más avanzadas como el aprendizaje automático para poder analizar los diferentes aspectos del juego y poder obtener ventajas competitivas. Este enfoque permite interpretar el juego con mayor precisión y profundidad, apoyando decisiones estratégicas tanto dentro como fuera del campo. El presente Trabajo de Fin de Grado se centra en el análisis del rendimiento en el fútbol profesional mediante el uso de técnicas de aprendizaje automático, con el objetivo de evaluar el impacto de diferentes métricas de tracking sobre el rendimiento colectivo de los equipos. En concreto, el análisis se ha realizado a nivel de selecciones nacionales, centrándose en partidos correspondientes a competiciones internacionales disputadas entre 2021 y 2024. Adicionalmente, la base de datos utilizada es StatsBomb Open Data con acceso a numerosos partidos de varias competiciones del mayor nivel futbolístico actual. A partir de la cual obtenemos los datos de tracking que nos permiten realizar el análisis de rendimiento. El desarrollo de este trabajo se ha realizado utilizando diferentes tecnologías, como entorno de desarrollo, se ha escogido Google Colaboratory. Además, el lenguaje de programación utilizado es Python, combinado con la importación de diferentes librerías reconocidas en el ámbito tecnológico del proyecto. title: A Process-Oriented Framework for Pattern Discovery in Professional Football: A Process Intelligence Approach
authors: Miguel José Janeiro Chaves Ferreira de Almeida
venue: Portuguese National Funding Agency for Science, Research and Technology (RCAAP Project by FCT)
abstract: Analysing collective behaviour in professional football relies on both event and tracking data, which share an inherently sequential nature.The computational approaches that exploit this, namely sequential pattern mining, process mining, network science, dynamical systems analysis, and machine learning, are dispersed across the literature, capturing distinct facets of collective behaviour.This fragmentation leaves practitioners without a unified means of extracting actionable patterns from a chaotic, adversarial environment, a difficulty compounded by the absence of an approach that orchestrates the complementary strengths of the available methods.This work addresses that gap through a Design Science Research approach.Firstly, the systematic literature review, conducted under the PRISMA protocol, characterises the state of the art by identifying the orchestration of existing approaches as the principal unmet need.This informs the design of a novel conceptual artefact, a layered framework for sequential pattern discovery built on an object-centric representation.The artefact is then refined through semistructured interviews with domain specialists, who assess its fit to professional practice by defining the requirements that a design derived from design alone could not supply.The interviews motivate the central revisions into the validated framework, replacing the fixed thresholds of prior work with context-relative formulations, elevating filtering and pattern selection to the core of the contribution, and treating the legibility of the output as a design objective.The result is TEMPO (Tactical Event-based Multi-method Pattern Orchestration), a novel framework that unifies the fragmented methods of the field on a single representation, governed by parameters that adapt

title: The Law of Unfair Dismissal and the Employment Rights Act 2025: An Opportunity Missed?
abstract: The right not to be unfairly dismissed has been a remarkably constant force in employment law since its introduction over 50 years ago. Unfair dismissal law was therefore overdue for some attention when the incoming Government was planning a major overhaul of employment rights, described as the ‘biggest single upgrade of employment rights in a generation’ and now implemented in the Employment Rights Act 2025. After strong opposition in the House of Lords, the Government moved to provide an amendedpackage, retaining a six-month qualifying period of employment and removing the upper limit on the compensatory award. In this contribution, I discuss the likely effects of these changes to the law, analysing the human rights implications of the Act and placing the amendments in a wider comparative context. I conclude that, although the Act holds great significance, particularly for those who would previously have been excluded from making any claim before the Employment Tribunal, they do not amount to the generational upgrade that may be seen in other areas of labour law. Severe deficiencies in the standard to which working people are protected from unjust dismissal decisions remain untouched by the new legislation. The Act is, perhaps, a once-in-a-generation opportunity missed. The right not to be unfairly dismissed has been at the centre of the protection of individual employees against the unjust use of the employer’s ultimate disciplinary power since its introduction in 1972. Given the scale of changes that have been made around it in the intervening period, in both individual and collective labour law, the law of unfair dismissal has remained remarkably constant. title: A framework for quantifying tactical team behaviour in Australian Rules Football
abstract: The inception of tracking technologies has allowed for increased access to the positioning data of team sport athletes. This information assists in understanding collective team behaviour by measuring the continuous movement patterns of players. Assessing the efficacy of collective team behaviour research requires comprehension of the contextual factors that may influence movement behaviour, such as the match phase and field location of the ball. Limited studies that have analysed collective team behaviour have accounted for such contextual variables. Research on collective team behaviour in invasion sports has typically focused on football and basketball, while investigations in Australian football (AF) remain largely absent. Furthermore, collective team behaviour investigations to date have generally inferred performance through the positioning of players without directly determining the continuous influence on match play. Therefore, this thesis presents new methodologies for measuring collective team behaviour in AF. This information was used to understand the extent to which collective team behaviour influenced match play in a continuous manner. The findings provide a framework to quantify tactical team behaviour in Australian Rules football (AFL). Global positioning systems (GPS) spatiotemporal datasets were obtained from match simulation sessions and elite-level AFL matches. This information was aligned with match event data to provide contextual information, such as match phase and ball location. Initial chapters investigated the collective behaviour of AF teams using a macroscopic approach during match simulation and a competitive match. title: Seeking conceptual clarity in the study of elite professional coaches and managers in rugby union and association football
abstract:
Introduction 
 
In this paper role clarification for elite men’s rugby union and association football coaches and mangers working in professional clubs within the UK is presented. The study’s sample is employers of elite coaches and managers, a population which hitherto have not been approached within the existing literature. Examination on how the roles are devised by the clubs is performed through identifying what attributes are perceived necessary for prospective candidates to uphold along with how these staffing structures are developed. The results of the present study contribute to a broader project focussing on the fast-tracking of elite athletes when transferring into elite coaching and managerial roles upon retiring from competing as a player in their respective sports. 
 
Method 
 
Employers of elite coaches and managers were theoretically sampled. The sampling criteria required individuals to currently be in a position in which they were central to the recruitment process for appointing coaching staff. Eight participants were sampled through conducting semi-structured interviews, four from rugby union and four from association football. All participants were at the time of interview employed by professional rugby union and association football clubs competing in the top three divisions of their respective sports. Data analysis consisted of initial open coding followed by axial coding. 
 
Results 
 
The results are presented in two categories; 1) roles and responsibilities and; 2) development and recruitment. Firstly, accountability for on field results transcended any other matter in respect for the manager’s roles. title: Reciprocal within-person associations between physical activity self-efficacy and enjoyment among primary school students participating in a cooperative games-based physical education curriculum: a four-wave random-intercept cross-lagged panel study
abstract: Introduction Physical activity self-efficacy and enjoyment are central to children’s motivation to be active, yet their temporal ordering and within-person interplay remain unclear. This study examined their reciprocal associations among 1,279 Chinese students in Grades 5 and 6 participating in a cooperative games-based physical education curriculum. Methods General physical activity self-efficacy and enjoyment were assessed on four occasions separated by 33, 28, and 28 days. Longitudinal measurement invariance was tested before conventional cross-lagged panel models and random-intercept cross-lagged panel models (RI-CLPMs) were compared. The primary RI-CLPM used class-clustered robust maximum likelihood and full information maximum likelihood for missing data. Results Scalar invariance was supported for both measures, and temporal equality constraints were not rejected. At the between-person level, average self-efficacy and enjoyment were positively correlated, r = 0.672, p < 0.001. In the retained equal-lag model, higher-than-usual self-efficacy predicted subsequent higher-than-usual enjoyment, b = 0.147, 95% CI [0.096, 0.198], βs = 0.146–0.154, p < 0.001. Higher-than-usual enjoyment also predicted subsequent self-efficacy, b = 0.088, 95% CI [0.026, 0.150], βs = 0.083–0.084, p = 0.005. The directional contrast was not significant, p = 0.063. Both associations remained positive in the corresponding complete-case model (n = 1,025), after class-by-wave mean adjustment, and under the specified missing-data sensitivity scenarios. Discussion The findings support reciprocal within-person temporal associations between general physical activity self-efficacy and enjoyment. title: A transformer-based multimodal fusion framework for ordinal motor skill-level assessment with biomechanical association analysis
abstract: Accurate motor skill assessment is essential for objective sports performance evaluation and data-driven coaching support. However, existing approaches often rely on single sensors, conventional classification models, or limited biomechanical interpretation, restricting their ability to capture comprehensive movement characteristics and ordered skill relationships. To address these limitations, this study proposes BioSkillFormer, a Transformer-based multimodal fusion framework for classifying badminton players into beginner, intermediate, and expert skill levels. The proposed framework integrates raw multimodal sensor sequences, timefrequency representations, biomechanical feature tokens, and reliability-aware cross-modal attention to capture complementary information from pose, electromyography (EMG), foot pressure, eye gaze, and video data. Skill-level prediction is formulated as an ordinal classification problem to preserve the natural progression of motor expertise. The framework was evaluated using the MultiSenseBadminton dataset under a subject-independent evaluation protocol. Experimental results demonstrated that BioSkillFormer achieved an accuracy of 0.8495, macro-F1 of 0.8375, balanced accuracy of 0.8420, ordinal mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.1560, and quadratic weighted kappa of 0.8530, outperforming single-sensor, timefrequency Transformer, and standard multimodal Transformer comparative methods. Ablation experiments indicated that ordinal loss, biomechanical tokens, timefrequency modeling, reliability-aware fusion, supervised contrastive learning, and masked modality reconstruction contributed to the observed performance. title: Neuromuscular Performance Thresholds to Support Player Development in a Professional Soccer Academy.
abstract: We aimed to compare neuromuscular performance between academy soccer players (U-17, U-19, and U-21 categories) and first-team players, and to establish neuromuscular performance thresholds associated with the first-team level. Ninety-four male players participated and were followed over two seasons. Neuromuscular performance was assessed using force-plate and force-sensing frame technologies, including isometric hip adduction and abduction, Nordic hamstring exercise, countermovement jump (CMJ), and isometric squat hold. Peak force, eccentric and concentric peak force, rate of force development, impulse, modified reactive strength index (RSI-modified), dynamic strength index (DSI) and limb asymmetry were analyzed. Linear mixed models, binary logistic generalized estimating equations (GEE), and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed. The neuromuscular variables that best discriminated between soccer academy and first-team were maximal hip pull force (OR = 2.53, p < 0.001), concentric peak force (OR = 2.42, p < 0.001), eccentric peak force (OR = 1.31, p = 0.046), modified RSI (OR = 2.00, p < 0.001), RFD at 200 ms (OR = 1.46, p = 0.004), and DSI (OR = 2.13, p < 0.001). ROC analysis identified practical cutoff values for maximal hip abduction force (442 N), maximal concentric and eccentric forces during the CMJ (1856 and 1804 N, respectively), modified RSI (0.58 m·s-1) and DSI (0.57). First-team players demonstrate superior neuromuscular performance to academy players. The identified cutoff values should be considered exploratory benchmarks for distinguishing current competitive levels and require external, prospective validation in independent cohorts from other clubs before practical application.

title: Group Cohesion and Salivary Oxytocin During a Six-Month Coordination-Based Training Program in Junior Handball Players: A Prospective Non-Randomized Controlled Intervention Study.
abstract: Whether coordination-based training can develop group cohesion in youth sport, and how cohesion relates to peripheral oxytocin, is unclear. We examined cohesion and salivary oxytocin during a six-month coordination- and cohesion-oriented program in junior handball players. Sixty-four male players (12-14 years) from four clubs joined a prospective, non-randomized, within-club controlled study (not prospectively registered). In each club, one pre-existing training slot (eight players) formed the experimental group (EG; n = 32) and the other the control group (CG; n = 32). For 24 weeks (three sessions/week), EG replaced 20-25 min of technical-tactical work with coordination, cooperation, and interpersonal-synchrony exercises. The primary outcome was Youth Sport Environment Questionnaire (YSEQ) Task Cohesion. In the baseline-adjusted, cluster-robust analysis, T1 Task Cohesion was 0.72 points higher in EG than CG (95% CI 0.22-1.23; p = 0.010); Social Cohesion differed similarly (adjusted difference 0.77 points; 95% CI 0.33-1.22; p = 0.003). The adjusted oxytocin difference was imprecise and non-significant (5.0 pg/mL; 95% CI -0.01 to 10.02; p = 0.050), and oxytocin change was unrelated to Task Cohesion change. The program was accompanied by a more favorable cohesion trajectory than time-matched standard training. Non-randomized allocation precludes causal conclusions; oxytocin findings remain exploratory.

title: Can Standardized Small-Sided Games Be Used as a Tool to Monitor Post-Match Fatigue in Male Academy Soccer Players?
abstract: This study aimed to analyze residual post-match fatigue using time-motion analysis across small-sided games (SSGs), fitness performance, and heart rate variability (HRV) in academy soccer players. Fifteen male academy players (18.3 ± 0.6 years) performed four SSG formats: 3 vs. 3 and 3 vs. 3 + 2 goalkeepers, played on small (25 × 18 m; 75 m2 per player) and large (36 × 25 m; 150 m2 per player) areas in a four-week experimental design. Two non-match weeks served as baseline weeks, and two weeks followed an official match. Time-motion during SSGs was monitored via GNSS. Before each training session (24, 72, and 120 h post-match), HRV, countermovement jump (CMJ) height, and maximum isometric force (MIF) of the hamstrings were measured. External load metrics were generally lower in post-match sessions than in non-match weeks; however, their low reliability limited the interpretability of SSG outputs. CMJ height was reduced, MIF was elevated post-match, whereas HRV showed distinct mid-week responses, decreasing in starters but increasing in non-starters. Post-match fatigue was evident in neuromuscular performance but was inconsistently reflected in SSG outputs. CMJ height reliably reflects post-match fatigue in male academy soccer players and should be prioritized when monitoring neuromuscular recovery.

title: Gender Differences in Pre-Service Physical Education Teachers' Visual Behaviour: An Eye-Tracking Study.
abstract: (1) Background: Teachers' visual attention is central to professional vision, yet whether teacher gender influences gaze allocation in Physical Education remains unclear. This study examined gender-related differences in visual attentional deployment when teachers observed students' motor competence, behavioural engagement, off-task behaviour, and gender. (2) Methods: Sixty pre-service Physical Education teachers observed video-recorded tasks from a class while wearing Tobii Pro Glasses 3. Fixation metrics were quantified across predefined areas of interest and compared between teacher genders. (3) Results: Female and male teachers showed comparable total and mean fixation durations. However, the former produced significantly more fixations during the closed task towards on-task students and with higher motor competence. Female teachers also showed higher fixation frequency regardless of whether off-task behaviour was successfully identified, and made more fixations towards both female and male students during this task. These differences were not consistently observed during the open task. (4) Conclusions: Teacher gender differed primarily with fixation frequency rather than fixation duration, and this effect was context-dependent. Additionally, greater visual sampling did not necessarily correspond to more accurate behavioural noticing. Mobile eye-tracking can reveal gender-related and task-sensitive differences in teachers' visual behaviour, with potential applications in Physical Education teacher education and professional development.

title: To Ensure Peak Velocity in Soccer, Coaches Should Stimulate Players to Run.
abstract: The aim of this study was to compare the peak velocities reached by professional soccer players during multiple training tasks and friendly matches, taking into account players' positions. Global positioning system data were obtained from twenty-three soccer players (age: 24.8 ± 4.1 years; body height: 180.3 ± 6.3 cm; body mass: 75.7 ± 5.0 kg) who played for the same professional first division team of the Spanish league (La Liga). The peak of velocity (km•h-1) of ten different training tasks was analyzed according to the players' position. The results showed that there were significant differences (p tactical velocity task (TVE, n = 53), friendly match (FM, n = 231) > large-sided game (LSG, n = 146) > medium-sided game (MSG, n = 273) > evolution task (EVO, n = 381), high interval intensity training (HIIT, n = 227), small-sided game (SSG, n = 407) > large-sided ball-possession game (LSBPG, n = 227) > small-sided ball-possession game (SSBPG, n = 316) and, 2) that in the tasks with lower peak velocities (MSG, EVO, HIIT, SSG, LSBPG and SSBPG), no differences were found in their positions. Therefore, different training tasks create different peak velocity demands, and tasks with higher peak velocities and role-specificity (TVE, FM, LSG, and MSG) require different needs from players in different positions.

title: Shooting accuracy and conditioning characteristics in proficient and non-proficient male perimeter basketball players: effects of distance and condition.
venue: Frontiers in sports and active living
abstract: Shooting accuracy is a key performance indicator in basketball, highlighting the importance of understanding how it varies with playing proficiency across different shooting conditions and distances. The present study had a three-fold aim to examine: i) the effects of shooting distance and condition complexity on shooting accuracy with respect to playing proficiency, ii) differences in shooting accuracy betwee playing proficient (PP) and non-proficient (NP) basketball perimeter players across different distances and conditions, and iii) differences in conditioning characteristics between PP and NP. The sample included 14 PP (age: 23.8 ± 3.4 years; body height: 189.4 ± 5.3 cm; body mass: 85.8 ± 5.6 kg) and 14 NP (age: 20.2 ± 2.0 years; body height: 182.7 ± 6.3 cm; body mass: 74.0 ± 10.2 kg) perimeter players. Three shooting conditions were assessed: stationary, dynamic, and competitive, across three distances (free-throw, two-point, and three-point). Conditioning characteristics were evaluated using a comprehensive battery of tests encompassing lower- and upper-body power, aerobic fitness, sprinting speed, change-of-direction speed, anaerobic capacity, and fatigue resistance. A binomial generalized linear mixed model examined all main effects and interactions. Independent-samples t-tests with Holm correction assessed differences in conditioning characteristics, quantified using Hedges' g. Even though PP showed greater overall shooting accuracy (p = .041), playing proficiency did not significantly moderate the effects of shooting condition or distance (all p ≥ .431).
